paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: a bill and account collector is not “someone who chases debts,” but an accounting position that verifies delinquency facts against records and compliance procedures, contacts debtors and negotiates repayment, posts payments to accounts, and leaves traceable evidence on records and disputes and authorization boundaries: locating and monitoring overdue accounts, verifying delinquency details using computers and automated systems, confirming the reason for delinquency in telephone or face-to-face communication and reviewing contract terms, persuading customers to pay credit card balances or loss claims or bad check amounts, arranging repayment or drawing up repayment plans based on the customer's financial situation, collecting payments and posting amounts paid to customer accounts, notifying the credit department or initiating property repossession or service disconnection procedures when the customer does not respond, tracing new addresses through post offices and telephone companies and credit reporting agencies or by asking neighbors, and retaining collection process and account status records; it is not suitable for people who only want to apply pressure and are unwilling to verify facts, are unwilling to constrain contact targets and times and frequency according to jurisdiction and institutional procedures, and are unwilling to write every contact and every repayment into a reviewable record.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to verify delinquency facts and contract terms clearly before speaking, you can repeatedly compare billing and repayment and reduction records on the same account item by item without omissions; you can stay restrained with emotional or repeatedly defaulting debtors and record every contact and result according to institutional procedures; you are willing to hand reduction and suspension and judicial referral matters you are unsure about to authorized personnel, and you can explain a repayment plan clearly in language the other party understands.

Conditions for pausing investment first: you have not yet completed a full verify-delinquency-facts—contact-and-confirm—negotiate-repayment-plan—post-payment—record-and-escalate loop under any supervised conditions, or you can only explain your interest by saying “I have made a few collection calls”; also do not treat familiarity with collection scripts or short-term recovery performance as proof that you can independently determine reductions and suspensions, or independently decide judicial referral and credit reporting authorization. Contact targets and contact times and frequency, the handling of debtor personal information and payment information, and the authority over reduction and suspension and judicial referral and credit reporting must be carried out in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and the competent authority and employer systems and must leave traceable records; this page does not provide any collection scripts, pressure tactics, or methods for circumventing regulation.

It must also be noted: the wage, employment, and industry data on this page are all under this occupation's separate definition on the O*NET page (the page does not contain labels such as “Wage data for …” or “Employment data for …” taken from another occupation). Education, occupational training, industry certification, employer hiring and job authorization, and the jurisdictional and institutional requirements on contact targets and times and frequency and personal information handling and reduction and suspension are different statuses and must be verified item by item according to employer and position and jurisdiction, and none can be automatically inferred from another.

In one sentence: this is an accounting and compliance position centered on verifying delinquency facts item by item and communicating and posting according to procedure, with the core being collection and account processing and repayment posting and record quality — not an imagination about “calling in debts”; its U.S. wage and employment are under this occupation's separate definition, growth is projected to be negative, and the contact practices involved are governed in the United States by the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA) and CFPB Regulation F.

The work of bill and account collectors can be divided into three categories: collection and account processing (locating and monitoring overdue accounts; verifying delinquency details using computers and automated systems; contacting delinquent customers by mail and telephone or in person; confirming the reason for delinquency in telephone or face-to-face communication and reviewing the terms of sales or service or credit contracts; persuading customers to pay credit card balances or loss claims or bad check amounts; arranging repayment or drawing up repayment plans based on the customer's financial situation and explaining necessary actions and repayment strategies; collecting payments and posting amounts paid to customer accounts; tracing new addresses for delinquent customers through post offices and telephone companies and credit reporting agencies or by asking neighbors); records and work order management (retaining collection process and account status records; recording address changes and clearing deceased customer records; organizing and filing correspondence and writing reports; verifying and updating account and repayment and reduction details; notifying the credit department of customer non-response and transferring account records as required); and notices and reconciliation and explanatory text (drafting collection and reconciliation and repayment confirmation correspondence; explaining account problems and repayment arrangements and consequences of default to customers; checking claim payment status with insurers and drafting appeal letters for denied claims; organizing reviewable explanations of billing and repayment and reductions). All three categories share the goal of writing “facts and basis and contact and result” clearly rather than obtaining repayment through pressure.

entries: Verifying delinquency | Give the claim a basis | Retrieve account and billing and repayment and reduction details, confirm the delinquency facts and debtor identity against contract terms and external information, and flag questionable items before contacting anyone.

Contact and communication | Keep contact compliant | Confirm the contactable targets and contact times and frequency according to institutional procedures, identify the institution and yourself, truthfully explain the matter and amount and consequences of default, and record the method and result of every contact.

Negotiation and arrangement | Make the plan executable | Hear the reason for delinquency, negotiate repayment or extension or reduction plans according to the customer's financial situation and the institution's authorization scope, explain necessary actions and follow-up milestones, and submit for approval when beyond authorization.

Posting and entry | Make payments verifiable | Collect payments and post amounts paid to customer accounts, verify billing and entry and reduction and extension records, and suspend and re-verify first when a discrepancy is found.

Records and filing | Make the process traceable | Retain collection process and account status records, address and contact changes, and correspondence and appeal materials, and retain and self-check record completeness as required by the institution.

Escalation and referral | Make responsibility transferable | When the customer does not respond or a dispute or complaint arises or credit reporting and account transfer and judicial referral are involved, transfer according to the authorization chain and record truthfully, and report immediately when unlawful debt or violence or intimidation or harassment is involved.

Billing and posting clerks are responsible for accurately entering and verifying bills and payments and adjustments and usually do not handle external contact or collection; bill and account collectors focus on contacting delinquent customers and negotiating repayment and posting payments and reductions and extensions to accounts.

If you prefer data entry and account verification and do not have to face customer emotions, compare billing and posting clerks first; if you prefer to communicate directly with customers and negotiate repayment after verifying the facts, bill and account collectors are suitable.

entries.answer: Contact delinquent customers by mail and telephone or in person and prompt repayment: locating and monitoring overdue accounts, verifying delinquency details using computers and automated systems, answering customer questions about accounts, confirming the reason for delinquency in telephone or face-to-face communication and reviewing the terms of sales or service or credit contracts, persuading customers to pay credit card balances or loss claims or bad check amounts, arranging repayment or drawing up repayment plans based on the customer's financial situation, collecting payments and posting amounts paid to customer accounts, notifying the credit department or initiating property repossession or service disconnection procedures and transferring account records to attorneys when the customer does not respond, tracing new addresses for delinquent customers through post offices and telephone companies and credit reporting agencies or by asking neighbors, checking claim payment status with insurers and writing appeals for denied claims, and at the same time retaining collection process and account status records and handling address changes and clearing deceased customer records.
entries.question: What do bill and account collectors do every day?

entries.answer: The key risks include legal liability for improper collection and harassment, leakage and misuse of debtor personal information, physical and emotional exhaustion from prolonged desk work and telephone work, errors in payment and reduction and fee and reconciliation records, out-of-control collection and dispute and complaint records, and unclear authority over collection and suspension and judicial referral; the control method is to first verify facts and contract basis, constrain contact targets and contact times and frequency according to the applicable jurisdiction and institutional procedures and identify yourself and disclose truthfully, handle debtor information under the principles of lawfulness and legitimacy and necessity, verify postings and entry item by item and retain traceable records, and stop when beyond authorization and hand reductions and suspensions and credit reporting and referral to authorized personnel.
entries.question: What risks should I pay attention to in advance for this job?

entries.answer: Look at reviewable output: whether you can verify delinquency facts and contract basis according to institutional procedures and leave traceable records, whether you can comply with the applicable jurisdiction's and institution's restrictions on contact targets and times and frequency during contact and disclosure, and whether you can stop and report when a dispute arises or the other party explicitly refuses contact or the situation exceeds authorization. The interest code CES and the skills and knowledge scores only indicate a similar direction and cannot replace this practical evidence.
entries.question: How do I judge whether I am suited to being a bill and account collector?

entries.answer: AI and automation can change account searches and delinquency detail summaries, call and work order summaries, repayment plan drafts and scheduling reminders, and reconciliation and report organization; but confirming delinquency facts and contract basis, judging contact compliance, actual communication and negotiation with debtors, and handling decisions on reductions and suspensions and credit reporting and account transfer and judicial referral are still borne by people. The degree of task automation does not equal a change in the number of positions; the official employment projection for this occupation is a decline (2024—2034 at -11%).
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Confirming delinquency facts and contract basis and debtor identity, judging the compliance of contact targets and times and frequency, actual communication and negotiation with debtors, posting and entry verification of payments and reductions and extensions, and determinations of whether reductions and suspensions and credit reporting and account transfer and judicial referral are feasible and whether unlawful debts or violence or intimidation or harassment are involved must be borne by you and authorized personnel according to the applicable jurisdiction and institutional systems; system output can only serve as a rollback-capable, reviewable assistance step.
entries.question: Which steps must retain human review?

entries.answer: Verify under six categories: education; occupational training; industry certification (O*NET lists only 7 national certifications, of which 6 are administered by ACA International and 1, Certified Professional Biller, by AAPC); institutional pre-job training and system and channel permissions; institution-internal authorization for contact and reductions and suspensions and credit reporting and account transfer and judicial referral; and the applicable jurisdiction's requirements on contact targets and times and frequency and personal information handling. paragraphs: FermatMind career content editorial team: based on the public occupational materials of O*NET and the U.S. BLS, the U.S. Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA) and U.S. CFPB Regulation F (12 CFR Part 1006), as well as the National Bureau of Statistics' Average Annual Wages of Urban Unit Employees in 2025, the China Banking Association's Guidelines for the Collection of Personal Consumer Loans by Financial Institutions (Trial), the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, and Article two hundred ninety-three, subparagraph one of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China; definitions, data periods, and usage limitations are labeled item by item. This page states only the scope of application and behavioral boundaries and does not provide any collection scripts, pressure tactics, or methods for circumventing regulation.

The main sources are O*NET occupation details, wages/trends/industry/job postings/training and certification catalogs for this occupation, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and the OEWS filed wage definition; the FTC legal introduction page is a summary, not the full regulatory text. For legal details, read the corresponding provisions of CFPB Regulation F. For China, read the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 wage tables and the total wage definition, the 54-article China Banking Association full text, the public text of the consumer law, and the court-attached Article 293, subparagraph one; for GB/T45251, only the official metadata was obtained.

Wages are 2025 OEWS; U.S. employment 2025—2035; the O*NET page footer updated 2026-10-06 and the current access is 2026-10-09. The industry page does not list a separate data year; posting technology comes from full-year 2025 U.S. postings; training is the IPEDS2025—26 catalog / 2024—25 completers. The association's January 30 release notice and the April 8 full-text web page dates are distinguished; Article 54 provides that it takes effect from the date of release. Regulation F cites the current provisions, and no single catalog revision date is used to claim that all provisions were uniformly revised most recently. GB/T45251-2025 was both released and effective 2025-02-28, metadata only.

U.S. occupational data differ from Chinese industry averages; gaps remain in precise Chinese occupational wages and specific hiring, personality validity, and AI adoption effects. U.S. Regulation F §§1006.1—2 applies to debt collectors that meet the definition and to consumer debts arising primarily for personal, family, or household purposes; there are exclusions such as employees of the original creditor collecting in its own name, and it cannot cover all commercial accounts or collectors. Specific business must also be verified against state law and other applicable rules. The China Banking Association guidelines are industry self-regulation: Articles 3—4 apply to member institutions' credit cards and personal consumer loans, requirements for external institutions should be written into the outsourcing agreement, and other personal loans may be referenced; the January 30 release notice and the April 8 full-text web page dates must be distinguished. Article 13 prohibits telephone calls, visits, and other collection from 22:00 to 8:00 the next day without consent; Article 14 states that when a call is not connected, attempts to the same contact method should preferably not exceed 6 times on the same day, unless otherwise agreed; Article 17 strictly prohibits collecting from unrelated third parties, and contacting them to obtain information has separate conditions for loss of contact, information boundaries, and restrictions after an explicit refusal. The official platform shows that GB/T45251-2025 Guidelines on Post-Loan Collection Risk Control for Internet Finance Personal Online Consumer Credit is a current recommended national standard, released and effective 2025-02-28, under the administration of the People's Bank of China. This round read only the official metadata and did not obtain the full text, so it cannot be claimed that all collection nationwide must implement its quantitative provisions. Legal provisions do not provide individual handling authorization, and editorial trials and position verification suggestions do not masquerade as current institutional systems.

Article 13 prohibits telephone calls, visits, and other collection from 22:00 to 8:00 the next day without consent; Article 14 states that when a call is not connected, attempts to the same contact method should preferably not exceed 6 times on the same day, unless otherwise agreed; Article 17 strictly prohibits collecting from unrelated third parties, and contacting them to obtain information has separate conditions for loss of contact, information boundaries, and restrictions after an explicit refusal. hero.quick_answer: Bill and account collectors contact delinquent customers by mail and telephone or in person and prompt repayment: locating and monitoring overdue accounts, verifying delinquency details using computers and automated systems, answering customer questions about accounts, confirming the reason for delinquency in telephone or face-to-face communication and reviewing the terms of sales or service or credit contracts, persuading customers to pay credit card balances or loss claims or bad check amounts, arranging repayment or drawing up repayment plans based on the customer's financial situation and explaining necessary actions and repayment strategies, collecting payments and posting amounts paid to customer accounts, notifying the credit department or initiating property repossession or service disconnection procedures and transferring account records to attorneys when the customer does not respond, tracing new addresses for delinquent customers through post offices and telephone companies and credit reporting agencies or by asking neighbors, checking claim payment status with insurers and writing appeals for denied claims, and at the same time retaining collection process and account status records and handling address changes and clearing deceased customer records; their work does not equal statutory collection compliance determinations or reduction and suspension decisions, nor does it replace the applicable jurisdiction's restrictions on contact targets and contact times and frequency or the institution's authorization and escalation requirements, and they stop and escalate when debtor identity or delinquency facts are in doubt, a dispute or complaint arises, or suspension and reductions and judicial referral exceed their authorization.

subject.name: Bill and Account Collectors
subject.summary: Bill and account collectors contact delinquent customers by mail and telephone or in person and prompt repayment: locating and monitoring overdue accounts, verifying delinquency details and answering customer account questions, confirming the reason for delinquency and reviewing contract terms, persuading payment and arranging repayment plans based on the customer's financial situation, collecting payments and posting amounts paid to customer accounts, notifying the credit department or initiating property repossession or service disconnection procedures when the customer does not respond, tracing new addresses for delinquent customers, checking claim status with insurers, and retaining collection process and account status records. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 43-3011.00 (Bill and Account Collectors), which is Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); the wage, employment, and industry data are all under this occupation's separate definition, the O*NET page does not state that they are taken from another occupation, and this occupation is not marked Bright Outlook; the employment projection is a decline (-1% or lower, with the employment trends page giving 2024—2034 at -11%). Collection practices in the United States are governed by the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA) and CFPB Regulation F. On the mainland China side, this page has not obtained a public occupational wage entry precisely corresponding to this occupation and shows only official proxies with clearly labeled industry and position category scope, and notes that collection practices in mainland China are governed by consumer rights protection rules, the industry norms of the national standard for post-loan collection, and the criminal law provision on the crime of collecting unlawful debts.
